questions.q: Which instruction of the Quran does the editorial quote on how to meet hurtful words?
options: “Complain to those in power”
Not quite. The article says: “Ignore their hurtful talk” – keep to one’s own good conduct whatever others say.
“Ignore their hurtful talk” – keep to one’s own good conduct whatever others say
Yes. This one-sided steadiness is called sabr, patience.
“Answer them in the same way”
Not quite. The article says: “Ignore their hurtful talk” – keep to one’s own good conduct whatever others say.
“Leave their land”
Not quite. The article says: “Ignore their hurtful talk” – keep to one’s own good conduct whatever others say.
questions.rationale: “The Quran has commanded believers to ‘ignore their hurtful talk’ (33:48). That is, irrespective of the negative response the other person gives, people of faith should in every situation unilaterally behave positively.”

questions.q: What does the article say the Quran teaches about how the prophets are to be regarded?
options: Only the prophets of one’s own people are to be honoured
Not quite. The article says: With equal respect – “We make no distinction between any of them”.
Later prophets are to be honoured above earlier ones
Not quite. The article says: With equal respect – “We make no distinction between any of them”.
Prophets are to be honoured according to the size of their following
Not quite. The article says: With equal respect – “We make no distinction between any of them”.
With equal respect – “We make no distinction between any of them”
Right. Jesus is honoured as a prophet with a miraculous birth.
questions.rationale: “One of the teachings of the Quran regarding prophets and messengers is: ‘We make no distinction between any of them.’ (3:84)”

questions.q: How does the Quran describe the followers of Jesus, as quoted in the article?
options: Their hearts were filled with compassion and mercy
They were great builders
Not quite. The article says: Their hearts were filled with compassion and mercy.
They were strict in law
Not quite. The article says: Their hearts were filled with compassion and mercy.
They were skilled in trade
Not quite. The article says: Their hearts were filled with compassion and mercy.
questions.rationale: “We gave him the Gospel and imbued the hearts of those who followed him, with compassion and mercy.”

questions.article: Help to a Seeker of Truth
questions.q: The article says God has revealed Himself in two “books.” What are they?
options: The Torah and the Gospel
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the universe – one His word, the other a practical demonstration of it.
History and philosophy
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the universe – one His word, the other a practical demonstration of it.
The Quran and the Hadith
Not quite. The article says: The Quran and the universe – one His word, the other a practical demonstration of it.
The Quran and the universe – one His word, the other a practical demonstration of it
Correct. Both are sources of spiritual inspiration.
questions.rationale: “God has revealed Himself in two books—the Quran and the universe. The Quran is a literal version of God’s word, while the universe, or nature, is a practical demonstration of it.”

questions.article: Help to a Seeker of Truth
questions.q: What lesson for his own conduct does a believer draw from seeing that every part of the universe behaves predictably and in harmony?
options: That he too should have a dependable character and live in harmony with others
Well read. Without hatred or malice.
That he has no freedom of choice
Not quite. The article says: That he too should have a dependable character and live in harmony with others.
That human society can never be orderly
Not quite. The article says: That he too should have a dependable character and live in harmony with others.
That nature should be left unstudied
Not quite. The article says: That he too should have a dependable character and live in harmony with others.
questions.rationale: “It is as if God was suggesting that he himself should have a predictable character… he should live in complete harmony with society, without hatred or malice towards anyone.”

questions.q: Which saying of the Prophet does the article quote to show that family life is a training ground for life in society?
options: “Speak good or keep silent”
Not quite. The article says: “The best of you is one who is best for his family”.
“Seek knowledge from the cradle to the grave”
Not quite. The article says: “The best of you is one who is best for his family”.
“The strong man is he who controls his anger”
Not quite. The article says: “The best of you is one who is best for his family”.
“The best of you is one who is best for his family”
Yes. A good spouse will prove a good citizen.
questions.rationale: “When a man and woman prove to be a good husband and wife, they will certainly prove to be good citizens… ‘The best of you is one who is best for his family.’”

questions.q: After a long debate with his student, what did Imam Shafi say to him when they next met?
options: “Let us never speak of this”
Not quite. The article says: “Would it not be better if we lived as brothers even if we cannot agree on any issue?”.
“Do not come to my lessons again”
Not quite. The article says: “Would it not be better if we lived as brothers even if we cannot agree on any issue?”.
“Would it not be better if we lived as brothers even if we cannot agree on any issue?”
Right. Differences were kept to the level of ideas.
“I was wrong and you were right”
Not quite. The article says: “Would it not be better if we lived as brothers even if we cannot agree on any issue?”.
questions.rationale: “Imam Shafi took hold of his hand and said: ‘Would it not be better if we lived as brothers even if we cannot agree on any issue?’”

questions.q: According to the article, what does the Quran set against patience as its opposite?
options: Silence
Not quite. The article says: Haste – acting on the spur of emotion.
Generosity
Not quite. The article says: Haste – acting on the spur of emotion.
Haste – acting on the spur of emotion
Yes. The patient act in line with nature; the hasty against it.
Courage
Not quite. The article says: Haste – acting on the spur of emotion.
questions.rationale: “According to the Quran (46:35), the opposite of patience is haste… those who fail are those who act hastily, driven by their emotions.”

questions.q: The article tells of a son who returned and fell at his father’s feet asking forgiveness. What is this story meant to explain?
options: The danger of leaving home
Not quite. The article says: True prostration before God – a heartfelt surrender that draws His mercy.
True prostration before God – a heartfelt surrender that draws His mercy
Exactly. It is more than a physical posture.
The duty of fathers to be strict
Not quite. The article says: True prostration before God – a heartfelt surrender that draws His mercy.
The value of good advice
Not quite. The article says: True prostration before God – a heartfelt surrender that draws His mercy.
questions.rationale: “True prostration is when someone, overwhelmed with emotion, lays his head on the ground… When a person surrenders to God in this manner, God’s mercy demands that He forgive him.”

questions.q: In what way does the article call the thought of death “positive”?
options: It frees a person from all responsibility
Not quite. The article says: It makes a person modest and realistic, gives urgency to good work and holds him back from wrong.
It makes a person modest and realistic, gives urgency to good work and holds him back from wrong
Well reasoned. “Every hero becomes a zero” before it.
It makes present pleasures sweeter
Not quite. The article says: It makes a person modest and realistic, gives urgency to good work and holds him back from wrong.
It shows that planning is pointless
Not quite. The article says: It makes a person modest and realistic, gives urgency to good work and holds him back from wrong.
questions.rationale: “Remembering death is the greatest source of wisdom for any person… in terms of the result it works as the greatest positive factor in the life of a person.”
